reviewed: November 2,2026 America/Los_Angeles: targeted primary-source checks across all 20 rows; scopes differ by publisher.
method: Initial research and per-vendor prior evidence remain retained. November 2 rechecks use publisher pages/support and default-branch GitHub README blobs. Not every secondary page was refreshed. Failed article fetches, ambiguous entitlements and conflicting plan/resource claims remain explicit. Documentation is not runtime, checkout, security, power or ranking proof.

vendors.name: Screenpipe
vendors.price: Free limited history; Basic $250/year (~$21/month); Business $500/seat/year (~$42/month); Enterprise custom.
vendors.license: Source available under a commercial license; source-based commercial/competing-product use is restricted. Official prebuilt builds have separate Terms of Service and plan terms.
vendors.features: Screen + mic/system audio; text-only Accessibility or pixels/OCR; local Whisper/Parakeet; history search; AI questions; local/Ollama and cloud providers; MCP; scheduled workflows/capture; app/window/URL scopes; publisher-advertised default form-field scrubbing; selected local text/image or enclave redaction; media-versus-text retention; personal device sync; managed seats; Enterprise SSO/MDM and shared context. Changelog also advertises calendar reminders, saved AI presets, timed starred sessions, custom MCP connections, clipboard context and narrated SOP exports.
vendors.difference: Capture, assistant context and automation reference. Business excludes shared teammate context. The plan table lists Max/Ultra beta access, while nearby prose singles out Ultra; exact entitlement and capacity prices need account/checkout verification.
vendors.caveat: Annual page defaults are not a tested checkout. Pricing estimates ~30GB/month and 600 MB–4GB RAM; architecture estimates 5–10GB/month/~600 MB, while current README says 0.5–3GB and 5–20% CPU. These are conflicting publisher estimates, not matched power/storage tests. The official CLI 0.4.53 keyword-HTTP result does not measure advertised desktop 2.7.84, capture, AI or audio. Enclave redaction sends selected raw text off-device; local storage alone does not make AI/sync/integrations local.
vendors.checked: November 2 primary pricing, AI/capture/privacy/storage/architecture docs, license, README and changelog; latest listed desktop 2.7.84 dated October 6. No vendor binary, checkout or redaction/power audit. Exact older benchmark source remains separate.

vendors.name: Original Rewind / Limitless
vendors.price: Wind-down: Pendant sales ended; continuing customers have free Unlimited through 2026. Desktop/web recording ended; historical meetings remain through 2026. Rewind capture disabled December19,2025.
vendors.features: Original Rewind combined screen/audio recall and AI retrieval. Limitless shifted toward meeting/lifelog transcripts and Pendant. Export can include transcripts, chats and audio.
vendors.difference: The authoritative legacy product reference, not an available new desktop competitor. Do not conflate it with rewind.app.
vendors.caveat: Meta acquisition confirmed. Account access/post-2026 support unverified; older help prices are not current availability. Distinct from rewind.app.
vendors.checked: November 2 official announcement and local-data help page; desktop/web recording unavailable, Rewind capture sunset, continuing Pendant support through 2026. Historical price/help details retain their prior scope. No account or runtime test.

vendors.name: Rewind Desktop (rewind.app)
vendors.price: Earlier publisher-article snapshot quoted $30/month; current homepage has no price and direct article fetch still fails. Current billing unverified.
vendors.license: Proprietary; distinct from original Rewind AI.
vendors.features: Always-on screen history; local OCR keyword search; full-screen timeline; global shortcut; private-window detection; H.264 compression; optional encrypted archive to user-owned S3 with on-demand older video.
vendors.difference: Visual replay and storage are its focus. Source says AI-powered search and meeting/audio transcription are not yet available.
vendors.caveat: ~2GB/week and low resource use are publisher claims. Search snapshots repeat $30/month, but do not verify current billing. Other-vendor descriptions in Rewind marketing comparisons are not evidence for those other vendors.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct homepage confirms local screen timeline/search and optional encrypted personal S3 archive; comparison article still cache-miss. This independent product is separate from original Rewind/Limitless. No checkout or binary test.

vendors.name: Pieces
vendors.price: Pro $18.99/user/month; Enterprise $22.99/user/month, or $69.99/user/quarter as displayed. Seven-day card-required trial; no free plan. Annual discount advertised without a freshly selected annual price.
vendors.features: On-device long-term memory across apps/websites; chronology and scoped recall; single-click standup, meeting prep and recaps; local/cloud model selection; unlimited MCP. Enterprise adds org capture/feature policies, approved providers and own API keys.
vendors.difference: Strong assistant/IDE context and prebuilt summary workflows. Enterprise governance is distinct from personal memory.
vendors.caveat: Do not reuse older free/$10 pricing or assume every model call stays local because memory is on-device. Vendor not run here.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct monthly pricing/model/BYOK table: 18.99 USD Pro, 22.99 USD Enterprise or 69.99 USD/quarter. Exact annual selection, billing and app runtime unverified.

vendors.name: Littlebird
vendors.price: Basic free; Plus $204/year ($17/month equivalent); Power $510/year ($42.50/month); Pro from $100/month. Team from $17/seat/month annual; Enterprise custom.
vendors.features: Active-window work context; bot-free meeting notes; chat, routines, hover, MCP and connected email/calendar/files. Free: 25 total meeting notes, 5 routines, daily credits. Plus: unlimited notes, up to 100 routines, MCP. Higher tiers expand credits/modes.
vendors.difference: Integrated actions and routines, with desktop/web/mobile access. Security page explicitly says context is encrypted and stored in AWS US East, not local-only.
vendors.caveat: Basic has daily credits,25 lifetime meeting notes,5 routines and2 Max messages/day. Plus trial requires a card. Power advertises2x Plus credits; selected Pro 5x starts$100/month, while the12x price was not selected. Unlimited notes do not mean unlimited AI. AWS/cloud and audit statements remain publisher claims.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct annual-default plans/limits and cloud-memory FAQ; selected Pro 5x quote only. No account, checkout or runtime/security audit.

vendors.name: Microsoft Recall
vendors.price: Windows feature on supported Copilot+ PCs; hardware/OS requirements apply. No separate Recall subscription documented in cited support.
vendors.license: Proprietary Windows feature; no macOS app.
vendors.features: Opt-in snapshots, timeline, semantic recall and source re-entry; on-device storage; Windows Hello/enclave security; app/site exclusions; private-browsing and sensitive-data filters; time/app/site deletion; storage management and enterprise policy.
vendors.difference: Reference for OS-level security, authentication and local inference. It does not record audio or continuous video.
vendors.caveat: Browser filtering is browser-dependent. NPU/security requirements limit hardware. Snapshot storage can pause below free-space thresholds. OSwind now has a managed disk-image vault; enclave security parity remains unproved.
vendors.checked: November 2 official support requirements/features recheck. Windows-only; no hardware purchase, account or runtime benchmark.

vendors.name: ScreenMemory
vendors.price: Free lists 24-hour history/single monitor, but also Unlimited History in the same card (conflicting). Standard $29 includes one year updates/3 devices; optional $5/year renewal. Lifetime $39 one-time.
vendors.features: Continuous screen recording; visual timeline; high-resolution playback; local OCR; app filters; calendar activity heatmaps; app blacklist; unlimited paid history; multiple monitors and three devices on Standard.
vendors.difference: Simple local visual recall with one-time pricing and a calendar-oriented interface.
vendors.caveat: Free card still contradicts 24-hour and unlimited history. Publisher FAQ says file access exposes recordings and encryption is planned; local storage is not an encrypted vault. No local RAG/audio/BYOK promise or runtime/energy qualification established here.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct homepage/pricing/FAQ; 29 USD Standard / 39 USD Lifetime unchanged. Free-history contradiction retained. No license checkout, runtime or storage benchmark.

vendors.name: TimeScroll
vendors.price: Free, open source.
vendors.license: GNU GPL v3 license text in the publisher repository (checked 24 October 2026); no TimeScroll code is embedded in OSwind.
vendors.features: Native Swift; local keyword and AI image/meaning search; highlights and app/date filtering; timeline; Accessibility direct mode; duplicate suppression; thermal backoff; MobileCLIP2 or Ollama embeddings; mic/system Whisper audio; MCP; app exclusions; encrypted vault with Touch ID/password (beta).
vendors.difference: A particularly relevant native, local, multimodal and energy-conscious competitor. OSwind has a managed vault and optional verified visual indexing; native authentication, energy and side-by-side acceptance remain open.
vendors.caveat: macOS 14+, Intel/Apple Silicon per publisher. Vault is beta. No downloaded binary or battery benchmark evaluated here.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct homepage feature/requirements recheck; encrypted vault still beta. Publisher claims only, no downloaded binary, security or battery test.

vendors.name: Retrace (haseab)
vendors.price: Free, MIT source.
vendors.features: Two-second configurable screen snapshots; Vision OCR; FTS/app/date filters; timeline; usage dashboard; Rewind import; hotkeys; HEVC encoding; highlights; app/private-window exclusion.
vendors.difference: Strong migration and visual replay reference. README distinguishes working HEVC from optimization work.
vendors.caveat: Very early development. Audio/Whisper is listed as disabled/coming soon, not shipped parity. Semantic search on website is coming soon.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob 3d2b854a137b); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: Retrace (jhammant)
vendors.price: Free source; no paid plan verified.
vendors.features: Local text + thumbnail history; native capture/OCR/embeddings/Foundation Models; hybrid search; timeline; AFK-aware stats; lock/idle stop; sensitive filters; timed hidden mode; retention; API/MCP; collectors for calendar, git, media and other context.
vendors.difference: Explicit local-only boundaries; no retained full-resolution raw frames; extensible per-app collectors. Separate project from haseab/retrace.
vendors.caveat: README claims are not independent validation. Source now describes Windows alongside macOS with differing capabilities.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob 5b35e6a1ea9c); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: rem
vendors.price: Free source.
vendors.features: Two-second screenshots/OCR; full-screen scrubber; text copy; keyword/app search; recent-context copy for LLMs; SQLite and video; purge-all; Intel build and basic multiple-monitor support.
vendors.difference: Small, inspectable early native implementation focused on rewind and text recovery.
vendors.caveat: README labels very alpha. Semantic/vector search, spatial search, more date filters, fine-grained purge and first-class multimonitor remain unchecked roadmap items.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob eb21245c7e1b); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: Unlost
vendors.price: Free source/download; no current paid plan verified.
vendors.features: Semantic memory search; natural-language date/app filters; Zoom/Meet transcript search; screenshot text crop/copy; open website from screenshot; SwiftUI frontend and local Python/txtai index.
vendors.difference: Reference for semantic retrieval and natural-language filtering rather than just keyword matching.
vendors.caveat: Local/provider LLM-agent integration and remote/cloud storage are explicitly unchecked future work. Repository feature claims were not run.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob 2e20b399872b); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: Pensieve (formerly Memos)
vendors.price: Free source; self-hosted infrastructure/model costs apply.
vendors.features: Passive multi-screen recording; local data control; full-text/vector search; chronological entity context; browser URL metadata; Ollama and OpenAI-compatible model endpoints; plugins; config UI; app blacklist; agent skill integration.
vendors.difference: Extensible Python/web architecture and configurable model processing. Renamed because Memos was already taken.
vendors.caveat: README says Mac/Windows, Linux in development. Local-only operation requires local endpoints/configuration; compatibility is not proof every external provider works.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob 567406f40389); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: Minne
vendors.price: Free MIT app; provider account/API charges or local Ollama separately.
vendors.features: Active-window text capture without screenshots; Markdown memory folder for people/projects/days/sources; contextual draft panel with explicit Insert; undo; memory chat; Claude/ChatGPT account or local Ollama; card/ID masking and password-field skips.
vendors.difference: Text-first memory and drafting with transparent, editable files. Avoids the visual archive and its storage cost.
vendors.caveat: Provider requests may send selected notes/context; local storage does not imply local inference. Optional daily version check. No screen replay parity intended.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct homepage: free MIT, text-only notes, explicit Insert/undo, own-provider or local Ollama data paths. No runtime or privacy-leak audit.

vendors.name: Omi
vendors.price: Current direct wearable offer: device $169 (reference $229); free unlimited on-phone transcription plus 300 cloud minutes/month. Pro $29.99/month or $269.91/year; first year $269 with kit, then $269.91/year. Older/search $129/$179 device quotes conflict. Mac desktop-only allowances/subscription applicability remain unverified.
vendors.license: Open-source ecosystem; inspect per-component licenses before reuse.
vendors.features: Mac/mobile/web audio capture, conversations and summaries, tasks, searchable memories, speaker profiles, custom vocabulary, templates, app integrations and MCP; optional wearable offline capture.
vendors.difference: Audio/real-world and wearable memory with broad integration ecosystem. Mac app can be used without buying hardware.
vendors.caveat: Do not equate self-hosting option with default app being local. Free Ask limits differ across landing pages; verify in app. Battery and compliance are vendor claims. Wearable pricing/transcription claims do not establish desktop subscription limits.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct wearable offer and official Mac/no-hardware/subscription help; 169 USD device / 269 USD first-year bundle / 269.91 USD renewal unchanged. Other monthly/on-phone allowances retain November 1 evidence. Mac-only entitlements and live stock/checkout remain unverified.

vendors.name: Granola
vendors.price: Basic $0; Business $14/user/month; Enterprise $35/user/month as rendered.
vendors.features: Bot-free device-audio notes; speaker tags; templates, multilingual notes and recipes; cross-meeting chat; shared folders; MCP; paid unlimited history, advanced models/integrations, prep and follow-up; Enterprise SSO, policy, SCIM/audit and admin controls. Voice typing is advertised in all plans.
vendors.difference: Meeting usability, team workflow and note quality reference; not an always-on visual desktop recorder.
vendors.caveat: Basic history is30 days, with MCP limited to personal notes in that window. Pricing says audio is deleted after transcription. Training opt-out differs between individuals and enterprise defaults. No capture, ASR, privacy or energy benchmark was run here.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct pricing/plan comparison; Basic 30-day MCP scope, paid API/integrations and Enterprise controls retained. No account, audio capture, ASR/privacy or billing test.

vendors.name: OpenRecall
vendors.price: Free AGPLv3 source; no subscription established in reviewed documentation.
vendors.features: Periodic screenshots, local OCR and semantic search, browser-based history/timeline, selectable local storage and primary-monitor-only option. Python 3.11; macOS, Windows and Linux.
vendors.difference: A portable Python/browser approach. The README recommends user-managed encrypted storage; this differs from an app-managed encrypted library.
vendors.caveat: Current README recommends an externally encrypted volume; app-managed vault encryption is not established. Earlier 2024 FAQ encryption roadmap remains historical. No source is incorporated into OSwind and no runtime/security audit was performed.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob 1b0c50a057e0); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: OpenHistory
vendors.price: Source and download described; no paid plan established in reviewed sources.
vendors.features: Permitted foreground Accessibility context without screenshots, audio or key logging. Searchable work timeline, hourly/day recaps, optional Apple on-device summaries or OpenAI/Anthropic/Kimi, authenticated read-only redacted MCP.
vendors.difference: Standalone text collection and optional summaries reduce reliance on screen pixels. Cloud use requires a chosen provider, key and transmission disclosure.
vendors.caveat: macOS 14+; Apple on-device summaries require compatible Apple Intelligence/macOS 26+. README contains both source-install and download language. Privacy, energy and distribution claims are not independently qualified.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct homepage/FAQ: Mac 14+, Apple 26+device-inference requirement, BYOK disclosure and redacted local MCP. Source-install/license details retain prior checks; no runtime audit.

vendors.name: silverfish
vendors.price: Source project; no subscription established. Local model/server resources are separate.
vendors.features: Foreground AX text/metadata, SQLite FTS5, local Ollama, four model slots with hardware-aware onboarding, hour/day/week summaries, graph/wiki/profile, chat, briefs, contextual rewriting and MCP.
vendors.difference: Text-only local-model architecture with separate model roles. Existing-database import and loopback-only inference are repository claims.
vendors.caveat: Apple Silicon/macOS, Rust/Xcode tools and running local Ollama per current API README. No energy, privacy, security, interoperability or runtime-ranking acceptance; connected MCP clients have their own data policies.
vendors.checked: November 2 connected GitHub API default-branch README claim check (blob 674e9f7d2735); selected lines and hash retained in source-check receipt. No build, runtime, energy or security qualification; license details retain prior evidence unless separately cited.

vendors.name: Goldfish (goldfish.sh)
vendors.price: Free during beta; post-beta price not published on reviewed homepage.
vendors.license: No open-source license established from reviewed primary pages
vendors.features: macOS/Windows AX text capture, local SQLite memory, contextual chat/replies, personalized summaries/wiki/profile/workflows, dictation and AI-tool connections.
vendors.difference: Local storage is separate from inference: policy describes Cloudflare/Azure AI processing for requests and background organization. It deliberately preserves common personal details for context.
vendors.caveat: Vendor policy, not an independent audit. Pattern masks are incomplete; names, emails, phones, addresses and DOB are not generally masked. Distinct from unrelated Goldfish coding-memory/forensic tools.
vendors.checked: November 2 direct homepage: free beta and Mac/Windows contextual replies/chat/integrations. Post-beta cost, model data handling and runtime behavior unverified.
